newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy economy may grow faster in 1997 - BOI.
newsitem.headline: Italy economy may grow faster in 1997 - BOI.

text.p: Italian gross domestic product may grow slightly faster in 1997 than it did last year, when it was estimated to have expanded by 0.8 percent, the Bank of Italy said in a six-monthly report.
"The rate of growth of the Italian economy in 1997 could prove to be slightly higher than that in 1996," said the report.
With Italy's exports performance showing signs of flagging, economic growth would depend on consumption by households picking up in the course of the year.
"In the light of the limited contribution expected from exports, such a prospect is subordinated to an acceleration during the year of consumption by families," the report added.

The central bank said the negotiation of new nationwide wage contracts would result in a substantial increase in labour costs in the coming months but these would be compatible with inflation of less than three percent.
"The renewal of the main national collective contracts and company agreements concluded until now have determined for the coming months significant increases in the cost of labour," it said.
"The scale of these increases is however compatible with an inflation rate of below an average of three percent," it added.
Monetary policy would be aimed at achieving a lasting fall in inflation, currently running at a year-on-year rate of 2.6 percent.

"The orientation of monetary policy remains targeted at making the fall in inflation durable, favouring an improvement in expectations and countering any emergence of risk factors," the Bank of Italy added.

Keeping the lira stable on the foreign exchange markets would play a key part in ensuring that inflation targets were met. The government hopes to keep consumer price inflation no higher than an average of 2.5 percent this year.
Although money market rates had fallen in the past year they were still high but lower inflation would help short term rates to decline.
"The interest rate differential with the mark is close to four percentage points in the short term and little more than 1.5 points in the long term," said the central bank.

"The consolidation of disinflation will facilitate the fall of rates even in the short term segment. To this end the achievement of substantial progress in the structural reordering of public accounts is essential," it added.
